newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Pre-Christmas rally seen for Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Pre-Christmas rally seen for Brussels bourse.

text.p: The Brussels bourse was expected to see a small rally ahead of the Christmas holidays as institutional investors were encouraged by Wall Street's rally and a firmer dollar.

"We could see a small rally before Christmas because New York is doing well, the dollar is strong and if volumes are small it would be easy to see a rally," said trader Paul de Lophem at broker Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
The Bel-20 share index closed up 0.39 percent, or 7.19 points, to 1,868.58 with volume swelling in afternoon trade to total 3.5 billion francs volume of Belgian shares traded.
Dealers expected the index to approach the resistance level of 1,900 on Friday or at the beginning of next week.
"Maybe 1,900 (Bel-20) for the first step and afterwards slightly above the 1,900 level...before Christmas," said de Lophem.
Another dealer said "there is still resistance at the 1,900 level in the market and we'll probably not pass this level (before year-end)".
But he agreed that "there could be a small year-end rally, probably tomorrow we'll see the expiry of options series which will create volatility in the market".
One dealer was not convinced of a pre-Christmas rally. "I wouldn't say rally, but the trend looks positive before Christmas".
Dealers said many investors had already closed their books before the year-end with only some large investors active.
"There's quite a lot of people who've already closed up their books but we've still got professional activity going on," one trader said.
Another dealer added that "we have more of a market where people are clearing their portfolio as the next settling date is January 8".
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert closed up 2.2 percent at 18,550 francs after a recent major-sell off which was spurred by a company 1996 profit warning.
One dealer expected the share to stay around current levels but added that "the share price is still too expensive".
Elsewhere chemicals and drug group UCB closed up 1.26 percent at 80,600 francs after touching an intraday high of 81,000 francs.
UCB's announcement after the bourse closed that 1996 would show profits, "significantly better than those of 1995", was likely to boost the share price on Friday.
